trans.sense: tip on a ribbon or cord
tip on a ribbon or cord

examples.text: Buckles and agglettes at vnwares, ſhall race his bowe, a thinge both euill for the fight, & perillous for freatinge.
examples.ref: 1545, Roger Ascham, “The Seconde Booke”, in Toxophilus, the Schole, or Partitions of Shooting […], [new] edition, London: […] Thomas Marshe, published 1571, →OCLC, folio 38, recto:

glosses: A tip, originally of metal and often decorative, on a ribbon or cord that makes lacing two parts of a garment or garments together easier, as in corset lacings, "points" (lacing hose or trousers to jacket or doublet) or sleeves to a bodice.

examples.text: a silken Camus […] Which all aboue besprinckled was throughout, / With golden aygulets, that glistred bright
examples.ref: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book II, Canto III”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London: […] [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:

glosses: An ornament worn on clothing, consisting of a metal tag on a fringe, or a small metallic plate or spangle.
